12 CFR 1016.7 Form of opt out notice to consumers ; opt out methods. ( a ) ( 1 ) Form of opt out notice. If you are required to provide an opt out notice under 1016.10 ( a ), you must provide a clear and conspicuous notice to each of your consumers that accurately explains the right to opt out under that section. The notice must state : ( i ) That you disclose or reserve the right to disclose nonpublic personal information about your consumer to a nonaffiliated third party ; ( ii ) That the consumer has the right to opt out of that disclosure; and ( iii ) A reasonable means by which the consumer may exercise the opt out right. ( 2 ) Examples ( i ) Adequate opt out notice. You provide adequate notice that the consumer can opt out of the disclosure of nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party if you : ( A ) Identify all of the categories of nonpublic personal information that you disclose or reserve the right to disclose, and all of the categories of nonaffiliated third parties to which you disclose the information, as described in 1016.6 ( a ) ( 2 ) and ( 3 ) of this part, and state that the consumer can opt out of the disclosure of that information; and ( B ) Identify the financial products or services that the consumer obtains from you, either singly or jointly, to which the opt out direction would apply. ( ii ) Reasonable opt out means. You provide a reasonable means to exercise an opt out right if you : ( A ) Designate check-off boxes in a prominent position on the relevant forms with the opt out notice ; ( B ) Include a reply form together with the opt out notice that, in the case of financial institutions described in 1016.3 ( l ) ( 3 ) of this part, includes the address to which the form should be mailed ; ( C ) Provide an electronic means to opt out, such as a form that can be sent via electronic mail or a process at your Web site, if the consumer agrees to the electronic delivery of information ; or ( D ) Provide a toll-free telephone number that consumers may call to opt out. ( iii ) Unreasonable opt out means. You do not provide a reasonable means of opting out if : ( A ) The only means of opting out is for the consumer to write his or her own letter to exercise that opt out right; or ( B ) The only means of opting out as described in any notice subsequent to the initial notice is to use a check-off box that you provided with the initial notice but did not include with the subsequent notice. ( iv ) Specific opt out means. You may require each consumer to opt out through a specific means, as long as that means is reasonable for that consumer. ( b ) Same form as initial notice permitted. You may provide the opt out notice together with or on the same written or electronic form as the initial notice you provide in accordance with 1016.4. ( c ) Initial notice required when opt out notice delivered subsequent to initial notice. If you provide the opt out notice later than required for the initial notice in accordance with 1016.4 of this part, you must also include a copy of the initial notice with the opt out notice in writing or, if the consumer agrees, electronically.

15 U.S. Code 1692e - False or misleading representations A debt collector may not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation or means in connection with the collection of any debt. Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, the following conduct is a violation of this section : ( 1 ) The false representation or implication that the debt collector is vouched for, bonded by, or affiliated with the United States or any State, including the use of any badge, uniform, or facsimile thereof.

( 2 ) The false representation of ( A ) the character, amount, or legal status of any debt; or ( B ) any services rendered or compensation which may be lawfully received by any debt collector for the collection of a debt.

( 3 ) The false representation or implication that any individual is an attorney or that any communication is from an attorney.

( 4 ) The representation or implication that nonpayment of any debt will result in the arrest or imprisonment of any person or the seizure, garnishment, attachment, or sale of any property or wages of any person unless such action is lawful and the debt collector or creditor intends to take such action.

( 5 ) The threat to take any action that can not legally be taken or that is not intended to be taken.

( 6 ) The false representation or implication that a sale, referral, or other transfer of any interest in a debt shall cause the consumer to ( A ) lose any claim or defense to payment of the debt; or ( B ) become subject to any practice prohibited by this subchapter.

( 7 ) The false representation or implication that the consumer committed any crime or other conduct in order to disgrace the consumer.

( 8 ) Communicating or threatening to communicate to any person credit information which is known or which should be known to be false, including the failure to communicate that a disputed debt is disputed.

( 9 ) The use or distribution of any written communication which simulates or is falsely represented to be a document authorized, issued, or approved by any court, official, or agency of the United States or any State, or which creates a false impression as to its source, authorization, or approval.

( 10 ) The use of any false representation or deceptive means to collect or attempt to collect any debt or to obtain information concerning a consumer.

( 11 ) The failure to disclose in the initial written communication with the consumer and, in addition, if the initial communication with the consumer is oral, in that initial oral communication, that the debt collector is attempting to collect a debt and that any information obtained will be used for that purpose, and the failure to disclose in subsequent communications that the communication is from a debt collector, except that this paragraph shall not apply to a formal pleading made in connection with a legal action.

( 12 ) The false representation or implication that accounts have been turned over to innocent purchasers for value.

( 13 ) The false representation or implication that documents are legal process.

( 14 ) The use of any business, company, or organization name other than the true name of the debt collectors business, company, or organization.

( 15 ) The false representation or implication that documents are not legal process forms or do not require action by the consumer.

( 16 ) The false representation or implication that a debt collector operates or is employed by a consumer reporting agency as defined by section 1681a ( f ) of this title.

15 U.S. Code 1692f - Unfair practices A debt collector may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect any debt. Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, the following conduct is a violation of this section : ( 1 ) The collection of any amount ( including any interest, fee, charge, or expense incidental to the principal obligation ) unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law.

( 2 ) The acceptance by a debt collector from any person of a check or other payment instrument postdated by more than five days unless such person is notified in writing of the debt collectors intent to deposit such check or instrument not more than ten nor less than three business days prior to such deposit.

( 3 ) The solicitation by a debt collector of any postdated check or other postdated payment instrument for the purpose of threatening or instituting criminal prosecution.

( 4 ) Depositing or threatening to deposit any postdated check or other postdated payment instrument prior to the date on such check or instrument.

( 5 ) Causing charges to be made to any person for communications by concealment of the true purpose of the communication. Such charges include, but are not limited to, collect telephone calls and telegram fees.

( 6 ) Taking or threatening to take any nonjudicial action to effect dispossession or disablement of property if ( A ) there is no present right to possession of the property claimed as collateral through an enforceable security interest ; ( B ) there is no present intention to take possession of the property ; or ( C ) the property is exempt by law from such dispossession or disablement.

( 7 ) Communicating with a consumer regarding a debt by post card.

( 8 ) Using any language or symbol, other than the debt collectors address, on any envelope when communicating with a consumer by use of the mails or by telegram, except that a debt collector may use his business name if such name does not indicate that he is in the debt collection business.

15 U.S. Code 1602 G- Definitions and rules of construction The term creditor refers only to a person who both ( 1 ) regularly extends, whether in connection with loans, sales of property or services, or otherwise, consumer credit which is payable by agreement in more than four installments or for which the payment of a finance charge is or may be required, and ( 2 ) is the person to whom the debt arising from the consumer credit transaction is initially payable on the face of the evidence of indebtedness or, if there is no such evidence of indebtedness, by agreement. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, in the case of an open-end credit plan involving a credit card, the card issuer and any person who honors the credit card and offers a discount which is a finance charge are creditors. For the purpose of the requirements imposed under part D of this subchapter and sections 1637 ( a ) ( 5 ), 1637 ( a ) ( 6 ), 1637 ( a ) ( 7 ), 1637 ( b ) ( 1 ), 1637 ( b ) ( 2 ), 1637 ( b ) ( 3 ), 1637 ( b ) ( 8 ), and 1637 ( b ) ( 10 ) of this title, the term creditor shall also include card issuers whether or not the amount due is payable by agreement in more than four installments or the payment of a finance charge is or may be required, and the Bureau shall, by regulation, apply these requirements to such card issuers, to the extent appropriate, even though the requirements are by their terms applicable only to creditors offering open-end credit plans. Any person who originates 2 or more mortgages referred to in subsection ( aa ) in any 12-month period or any person who originates 1 or more such mortgages through a mortgage broker shall be considered to be a creditor for purposes of this subchapter. The term creditor includes a private educational lender ( as that term is defined in section 1650 of this title ) for purposes of this subchapter.

12 CFR 1026.11 - Treatment of credit balances ; account termination.

( a ) Credit balances. When a credit balance in excess of {$1.00} is created on a credit account ( through transmittal of funds to a creditor in excess of the total balance due on an account, through rebates of unearned finance charges or insurance premiums, or through amounts otherwise owed to or held for the benefit of the consumer ), the creditor shall : ( 1 ) Credit the amount of the credit balance to the consumer 's account ; ( 2 ) Refund any part of the remaining credit balance within seven business days from receipt of a written request from the consumer ; ( 3 ) Make a good faith effort to refund to the consumer by cash, check, or money order, or credit to a deposit account of the consumer, any part of the credit balance remaining in the account for more than six months. No further action is required if the consumer 's current location is not known to the creditor and can not be traced through the consumer 's last known address or telephone number.

( b ) Account termination.

( 1 ) A creditor shall not terminate an account prior to its expiration date solely because the consumer does not incur a finance charge.

( 2 ) Nothing in paragraph ( b ) ( 1 ) of this section prohibits a creditor from terminating an account that is inactive for three or more consecutive months. An account is inactive for purposes of this paragraph if no credit has been extended ( such as by purchase, cash advance or balance transfer ) and if the account has no outstanding balance.

( c ) Timely settlement of estate debts ( 1 ) General rule.

( i ) Reasonable policies and procedures required. For credit card accounts under an open-end ( not home-secured ) consumer credit plan, card issuers must adopt reasonable written policies and procedures designed to ensure that an administrator of an estate of a deceased accountholder can determine the amount of and pay any balance on the account in a timely manner.

( ii ) Application to joint accounts. Paragraph ( c ) of this section does not apply to the account of a deceased consumer if a joint accountholder remains on the account.

( 2 ) Timely statement of balance ( i ) Requirement. Upon request by the administrator of an estate, a card issuer must provide the administrator with the amount of the balance on a deceased consumer 's account in a timely manner.

( ii ) Safe harbor. For purposes of paragraph ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ) of this section, providing the amount of the balance on the account within 30 days of receiving the request is deemed to be timely.

( 3 ) Limitations after receipt of request from administrator ( i ) Limitation on fees and increases in annual percentage rates. After receiving a request from the administrator of an estate for the amount of the balance on a deceased consumer 's account, a card issuer must not impose any fees on the account ( such as a late fee, annual fee, or over-the-limit fee ) or increase any annual percentage rate, except as provided by 1026.55 ( b ) ( 2 ).

( ii ) Limitation on trailing or residual interest. A card issuer must waive or rebate any additional finance charge due to a periodic interest rate if payment in full of the balance disclosed pursuant to paragraph ( c ) ( 2 ) of this section is received within 30 days after disclosure.

I then pointed out specific evidence to TransUnion, which I included within the 60 pages of attachments, and explained there is no possible way this alleged debt could be accurate for the following reasons : 1. n according to your rating key for XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX?

I recorded the phone call, including Transunion 's permission, stating, " All calls may be recorded. '' I also had that recording transcribed and attached it here for your review. ( See Exhibit IV. As you can see, TransUnion is still reporting a date open of XX/XX/XXXX and states the estimated month and year this item will be removed is XXXX/XXXX. - Despite this timely dispute, the debt was reported to the credit bureaus on XX/XX/XXXX, without proper validation, which is a direct violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 and 1681i.

Key Issues : 1. Violation of Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) - 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 and 1681i : - Columbia Debt Recovery LLC reported the disputed debt to the credit bureaus before resolving the dispute. The FCRA mandates that companies not report inaccurate information and promptly correct any inaccurate information. By reporting the debt without proper validation, the debt collector has failed and continues to fail to adhere to these requirements. 
- Furthermore, under FCRA Section 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 7 ), the debt collector was required to notify me in writing about the negative information furnished to the credit bureaus. I did not receive such notice, which further constitutes a violation of the FCRA.

2. Violation of Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) - 15 U.S. Code 1692g : - - I obtained the Notice to Vacate document from XXXX XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. The Notice to Vacate document was signed by both parties, indicating that the lease was fulfilled without additional fees. Columbia Debt Recovery LLC has never provided written validation of the debt. Furthermore, providing validation before receiving the dispute notice from a consumer can not be an excuse to ignore their obligation to validate the debt upon receiving the dispute. 

3. Violation of California Civil Code Section 1950.5 : - California law requires landlords to provide an itemized statement of deductions within 21 days after the tenant vacates the property. I did not receive the itemized statement within the legally required 21-day period. The 21-day requirement is designed to protect tenants from unjust charges and to ensure transparency in the handling of security deposits. Failure to provide timely and documented proof of mailing undermines this protection, resulting in potential harm and unfair treatment as a tenant.

After many cycles of disputes and investigations ( Ive sent in full documentation ) by Goldman Sachs they insist that the merchant charges remain. My balance should be XXXX and I should owe them nothing. 

Here is the story from the beginning. 


On XX/XX/XXXX I ordered a XXXX XXXX XXXX with extra RAM. ( total cost was {$1000.00} ) At the time, I responded to the offer to apply for an Apple Card ( Goldman Sachs ) for that purchase and was approved. 


I received the new computer, but it soon become obvious that it was not charging for some reason, so I brought it to my nearby Apple Store to have it looked at.

The specialist at the Apple Store looked at my computer and said that it was XXXX and that it needed to be replaced. They said that Id have to arrange to ship it back t

o Apple myself because it was a custom order with extra RAM which they do not in stock in the stores. Well, went home and called Apple to ar
range the exchange of my computer.

I was able to ship it back, and Apple received my return but after that, something went wrong on Apples end, and I never got my replacement computer.

After several calls with Apple to try to get to the bottom of it, I finally got someone ( a supervisor or manager ) who said that they would just go ahead and completely cancel that order and then I could then go online and just purchase a new computer from scratch. 
I wound up not purchasing a new computer at that time and I soon cancelled my Apple Card. 

The ONLY thing I used the Apple Card for was to order that one laptop which was returned ( along with the gift card I never used ). Again, the order was cancelled and refunded to the card by Apple.

I have documents showing my order, showing that Apple received the return, and that the card was refund was being processed. Goldman Sachs has continually insisted that I owe them for this computer. I have filed more disputes than I can remember ( at least six ) and have spent more hours on the phone with them than I can possibly add up. I have sent them all the documentation that I have many times, yet they keep coming back at me saying that after investigation, there was no billing error, and the merchant charges will stay on my account. 
This has been going on since last XXXX ( it is now XX/XX/XXXX ). The last time I spoke to anyone at Goldman Sachs I was bounced around on conference calls between Apple and Goldman Sachs for three hours ( Apple confirming the accuracy of my claim ) only to be hung up on by someone at Goldman Sachs who told me that there was nothing that could be done. 

Bottom line is that in the end I never bought anything with my Apple Card and there should be XXXX balance on it. 

There is no other way I can try to remedy this with Goldman Sachs. I keep filing disputes and sending in the proof of my claim and they just keep coming back at me saying that I am wrong and that I owe them for this computer. What else can I do? 

Please help me end this nightmare with Goldman Sachs.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Hello, I am on an IDR plan ( PAYE ) to repay my federal consolidated student loans through Mohela. When loan payments resumed in XX/XX/XXXX, my monthly loan payment was {$380.00}. 

In late XXXX, I started receiving multiple correspondence from Mohela indicating that I should recertify my income and family size to avoid missing my recertification deadline of XX/XX/XXXX. I recertified my income with Mohela on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received correspondence from Mohela that my new monthly loan payment would be {$1100.00} as a result of the recertification! This new payment would be due XX/XX/XXXX. I began anxiously planning how I could change my life in order to accommodate this payment. 

Within days of my recertification, the Biden administration announced that the deadline to recertify income and family size for IDR plans would be extended until XX/XX/XXXX, and therefore the earliest anyone would have to recertify to meet the deadline would be XX/XX/XXXX. The announcement acknowledged that if you already recertified, and your payment went up, it would be reverted to its previous monthly amount ( ie. {$380.00} for me ), until the new recertification deadline. ( See : https : //studentaid.gov/announcements-events/idr-recertification-extended ). 

I became aware of this announcement midXXXX, and first called Mohela XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXX ). The agent confirmed that, due to the announcement, the new payment of {$1100.00} would *not* go into effect in XX/XX/XXXX. Instead, I should expect to continue {$380.00} monthly payments until at least XX/XX/XXXX, as noted on studentaid.gov. The agent confirmed that she put in a request to have my monthly payment lowered back to {$380.00} per month. She said the turn-around would be 5-7 business days. Then, I should get a letter posted to my account with the updated monthly payment. If this were true, this should have occurred well before my XX/XX/XXXX loan payment due date. 

I called Mohela again XXXX because the payment amount still was not updated. It showed I would owe {$1100.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. I called Mohela and was on hold for XXXX hour and 46 minutes before I had to give up. I was unable to speak with an agent that day. They had a recording that best times to call, for lower call volumes, were Thursday and Friday mornings. 

I called Mohela again on Thursday morning, XXXX. The first agent I spoke with told me that they saw documentation from XX/XX/XXXX regarding a request to return my monthly payment to the prior amount. However, they told me, the request did not go through. The agent said, maybe they missed a step?. They transferred me to another agent. The second agent I spoke to agreed that my monthly payment should be returned to the prior amount of {$380.00}, in accordance with the Biden administration announcement. She said that she would request, again, to have my payment correctly lowered. However, it will take some time to go through. She was not able to give any time estimate. She did advise me that I would need to make my monthly Mohela payment on time ( ie. the EXACT amount listed on the account, whether or not its correct ), in order to ( a ) prevent my account from going into forbearance and ( b ) prevent my monthly payment from not being counted towards PSLF. She said that if I ended up overpaying, I could call Mohela to request a refund later. She stated that there was no designated form, or other information regarding the refund process. She said I should simply call. 

This request did not go through in time, so I paid Mohela {$1100.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. This was an overpayment by {$710.00}. 

I called Mohela again on Thursday morning XX/XX/XXXX to check the status. The agent acknowledged that my monthly payment should be {$380.00}. They were " unable '' to provide the status of my prior request to lower my payment, so they said they would put in *another* request to lower it back to the correct amount. This time, they said it could take up to 60 business days. In the meantime, they confirmed I would have to continue submitting monthly payments in the exact amount listed on the account to prevent forbearance or disqualification of my payments for PSLF. 

I called Mohela again on Thursday morning XX/XX/XXXX to check the status of my request, since it seemed that all prior requests had failed. This time, the agent confirmed that my request was in process to have the monthly payment lowered from {$1100.00} to {$380.00}. They also confirmed that it can take 60 business days from the date of request. If this time frame is correct, that means my payments might not be lowered to the correct amount until approximately XX/XX/XXXX! Then, the kicker. This agent informed me that I cant apply for a refund of overpayments later on, if my account was not put into forbearance at the time. This made no sense to me, since the prior agent I spoke to clearly stated that I would be reimbursed in the future for any overpayment related to this premature recertification. Also, if my account is put into forbearance, it would disqualify any payments made during that time from PSLF. I declined forbearance for this reason. The agent said there was nothing they could do. 

I paid Mohela {$1100.00} again on XX/XX/XXXX. This was another overpayment by {$710.00}, for a running overpayment total of {$1400.00}. Mohela currently has my account listed as owing {$1100.00} again on XX/XX/XXXX. Please help. I should not have to pay a higher amount due to Mohela not following the new guidelines to delay income and family size recertification. It is unfair for me to be punished for trying to do the right thing when I recertified prematurely, as instructed by Mohela. 

As you can see, I have called Mohela numerous times, but they have not been able to offer acceptable solutions, especially when my future hangs in the balance. They seem happy for me to continue making large overpayments, and they do not seem to care that their purported turn-around time of XXXX business days is a major financial hardship for me. I am not even sure whether they will fix the problem in that time frame since they have been incredibly unreliable. And, perhaps most frighteningly, they have now indicated that they would not refund me in the future for overpaying, as they had previously stated they would. I dont know what to do. This is not a financially sustainable situation for me. Please help me get my monthly payments correctly lowered. Please help me get reimbursements for my overpayments. Thank you. I really appreciate your help.

Consumer complaint narrative: On Monday, XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX I purchased a pair of {$600.00} XXXX  XXXX ( discounted to {$180.00} pre-tax ) from XXXX using PayPal 's Pay-in-4 split pay feature, using my XXXX XXXX as the funding payment method. I placed my order and went about my day. The next day, Tuesday XX/XX/XXXX, my order shipped via XXXX. The XXXX tracking number provided was XXXX. The package was picked up by XXXX on Tuesday, XX/XX/XXXX, and was out for delivery Wednesday, XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXXXXXX XXXX The package was delivered at XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX without any kind of signature confirmation required. I was at work all day, but I was aware that a delivery had happened. At about XXXX XXXX., an unknown person was let into the apartment building by a neighbor who was exiting for a smoke. This man went to the 5th floor via the elevator and then walked down to the 4th floor from the 5th floor, appearing to be scanning the area. for packages. He went down to the third floor, and then made his way to the second floor where I live and he located my package. On my XXXX  camera, as well as on multiple different high quality cameras that the building was kind enough to provide me with, he was caught on camera taking the package into the staircase between the second and first floor, opening the package and removing my items, and then disposing of the shipping box in the third floor trash room. He then left the building. I was not aware that a theft had occurred until I returned back home from work around XXXX XXXX that day. When I noticed that there was no package in front of my door nor in the lobby by the mailboxes, I immediately opened my XXXX  camera and looked to see if there was anything abnormal. I then found footage of the theft. I called the local police precinct to ask them what I should do and they informed me to call XXXX  and to file a police report with officers. I did so. After compiling the video footage from my own XXXX camera as well as from the building, alongside the official police report, I reached out to XXXX the same night as the theft. I spoke to somebody on the phone and explained the situation, and a claim was opened with XXXX  to investigate further steps. I was under the impression by the agent I spoke with that I would be protected by XXXX because I had not received my order and this was not my fault. I had even asked the representative what would happen if the claim was denied by XXXX  to which I was told, " don't worry, XXXX will take care of you.. From then on, I was not too concerned. The next day, a detective from the XXXX visited my apartment while I was at work. We spoke over the phone since I was not there to answer the door for him. We discussed the events that happened and I provided him with all of the footage I received, which he then had added to my police report filing. I was informed that facial recognition is going to be run on the thief, since we had such high quality video including multiple full-face angles. I continued to not be too concerned because I was under the impression that I was protected financially for this loss by either the merchant, the payment processor or my credit card company. Later on that evening of Friday the XXXX, I received an email from XXXX informing me that the claim was rejected by XXXX due to the package showing as delivered and that XXXX was refusing to take responsibility for the stolen package. I was shocked to read this, so I reached out to PayPal where I made my purchase through knowing they had buyer protection. I explained the situation and was met with very similar verbiage that they will not be responsible for a package being stolen. I was baffled that their buyer protection policy, that specifically states if you did not receive your purchase, you will be protected and issued a refund. I was very shocked to hear that PayPal 's buyer protection did not have my back as they have advertised. I reached out to XXXX, who was the funding card for my split pay plan, and was met with the same answer. I called XXXX again and was told the same thing. I was told to continue working with law enforcement, which I am, however I am confused how buyer protection for not receiving your order does not apply to a theft that was very much not in ones control. I do not live in a single family home where someone can just walk up to a porch and walk away with a package, this thief trespassed on the property and I was not home or able to protect myself or the package from the theft. I am currently out exactly {$190.00}. The investigation is still ongoing with the XXXX for the theft, although I am less confident of a positive outcome, as I have seen the responses I received from the merchant, payment processor, and credit card company essentially blaming me for being robbed. What I am seeking is financial relief in the amount of my purchase price from some kind of consumer protection insurance clause that will protect me from this unforeseeable financial loss that was well beyond my reasonable control.

New York State Laws 1. New York General Business Law ( GBL ) 601 : This statute prohibits the use of false or misleading information in the collection of debts. It also mandates that consumers must be provided with clear and accurate information regarding their debts.

2. New York Fair Credit Reporting Act : Similar to the federal FCRA, New York States version ensures that credit reporting agencies operating within the state maintain accurate records and provide consumers with access to dispute and correct any inaccuracies in their credit reports.

I requested that they immediately freeze my account and investigate the matter. The fraud department representative said the system could not verify my identity and could not provide details about my account. I was extremely worried. 

The next day XX/XX/XXXX was a national holiday. Banks were all closed. I was still unable to check my account.

She immediately emailed the check department to request that they stop the transactions. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a call from the branch manager of Citibanks XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. She informed me that the two official checks had been deposited into another bank by the criminal. 

Banks have legal obligations and fiduciary duties to ensure the safety of customers funds, but Citibank has failed to fulfill these. 

Citibank has significant deficiencies in preventing fraudulent transactions : XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I noticed the fraudulent activities and promptly reported it to the fraud department. However, due to Citibanks XXXX  identity verification system, my cell phone number, which had been in my name for more than 10 years, couldnt receive the verification code, which delayed the action in response to the fraud. 

XXXX. Although they could not verify my identity during the phone call, they had been alerted to the fraud and could have temporarily frozen the two official checks. Despite my multiple requests to freeze the account, they failed to do so. They did not take any actions to prevent the development of the fraud, missing the chance to recover the loss.

XXXX. Citibank failed to make sufficient efforts to stop the fraudulent transactions timely, resulting in preventable losses. It allowed the criminals to succeed, which would encourage them to continue committing crimes. This is extremely detrimental to our society and community. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I successfully set up the case with the XXXX after making 7 attempts at 3 different XXXX offices and immediately mailed the case number to the Incident Reporting Unit at Citibank. Consumer complaint narrative:
[ Complaint Regarding TD Bank ] In XXXX I sent a check for my next month 's rent, and this check was cashed in XXXX. On XXXX XX/XX/year>, I learned from an intermediary of my landlord that they had not received the check I sent for my XXXX rent. Circumstantially, it appears that my check was stolen in the mail and then cashed improperly. 

The institution which cashed the check, which I believe is TD Bank based on communication with my own bank, appears to have behaved extraordinarily recklessly. The individuals who cashed this check seem to have failed to take even the bare minimum standard of caution with regard to verifying whether what they were doing was reasonable. ( a. ) The endorsement of the check clearly does not match the person that the check was made out to. The check was made out to my landlords, but the endorsement on the back of the check obviously does not match either of these names, ( b. ) The amount the check was cashed for does not match the payment specified on the front of the check. The check is clearly marked for " XXXX '' and " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX' but, in spite of this, the check is cashed for {$650.00} dollars. 

I took this claim to my bank, who informed me that I would need to fill out some sections of a form and that the payees ( i.e. my landlords ) would need to fill out other sections. While I was trying to deal with the forms my bank gave me for my improper check endorsement claim, another problem appeared. 

On XXXX XX/XX/year>, the front desk of my apartment building attempted to return a credit card to me, a Target XXXX which they believed I had lost. I had never seen this credit card before, and the name on the card was not quite right. The name on the card has the same first name as me, the same middle initial as me, and a last name which is one letter off from my own last name. The XXXX was issued by TD Bank, who I knew had improperly cashed my stolen check. Given that prior stolen check, I suspected that the reason for this card was not because of a coincidence but because someone might have fraudulently used my stolen information to open a credit card with a misspelling of my name. 

This Target XXXX issued by TD Bank worried me a great deal, and I began to be afraid that what seemed like just a simple stolen check might be the prelude to more involved financial wrongdoing. I decided to visit TD Bank to determine why I seemed to constantly encounter new misfortunes linked to their bank. 

When I visited a TD Bank branch location at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX NY XXXX XXXX the afternoon of XXXX XX/XX/year>, TD Bank personnel were not able to provide any helpful information on anything. They were not able to determine whether it was the case that I was the supposed recipient of the Target XXXX with the name line being a misspelling. Nor were they able to escalate this quite serious possibility of financial impropriety on multiple fronts in any helpful way. The only recourse they suggested to me was to attempt to foist me on to various other parties such as my own bank or Target. 

I am in the process of trying to convince my landlords to cooperate with my bank 's investigation and I did in fact go to a Target store. However, there is important information about the improper check cashing that I think only TD Bank can provide, and Target has been of dubious help. At the Target store I was informed that the Target store branches have also decided they have no responsibility in this ; they determined I needed to call a Target phone number. Calling the phone number led to a redirect, which led to the call abruptly hanging up on me. 

I am requesting the following : - I would like TD Bank to provide law enforcement all information about this improper transaction available to them. I do not believe there are any circumstances in which it is lawful for a check to be cashed for an amount that does not match the value of the check by reason of an endorsement that does not match the recipient of the check, so I am unsure on what grounds it could be legitimate for TD Bank to avoid notifying and fully cooperating with law enforcement. 
- An escalation pathway from TD Bank to handle this strange and worrying credit card that has been found. I think this escalation pathway should be handled by TD Bank, which has taken on the responsibility of issuing the credit card, rather than being displaced onto various other parties for the purposes of TD Bank 's convenience.

Consumer complaint narrative: Yesterday, XX/XX/XXXX I received a call from XXXX Judgment Solutions ( " FJS '' ). I spoke with a man who said his name was XXXX. He said that FJS is not a collection agency, but a mediation agency. He told me that I owed money from XXXX XXXX. I asked him for details concerning the debt. He said that I was sent a letter in the mail and that my only option to avoid being served at my home or place of employment was to enter into remediation. He said that FJS is in XXXX Wyoming. He said that the debt was from a XXXX XXXX chargeoff account. I contacted XXXX explained that I received a call from FJS and asked if I owed money to XXXX. I called FJS again and conferenced XXXX into the call. XXXX said he would consult with the legal department and return my call. I did not receive a return call but later spoke with XXXX XXXX XXXX who said that she would speak with the legal department and see what they could do to reduce the debt, but that the letter would be e-mailed to me. When I opened the email it came from the email address case management and was a docusign document - not FJS. I did not open the attachment because I was expecting a letter from FJS. XXXX XXXX called me repeatedly telling me my home phone number and address was proof that I owed the debt. I told her that was my previous phone number and address but that did not prove that I owed money. I asked her if she could provide me proof of the debt ( i.e. bills - she said they are not a collection agency ). She said that once we go to trial the bills and proof of the debt will be provided to me, but that if I choose to go to trial an additional cost of {$2500.00} will be added to amount owed - or she could help me out if I accept remediation. My home phone number and address are public information. That does not prove that I owe a debt. I provided FJS my email address so that they could forward me the correspondence I never received. If someone owes a legitimate debt then FJS should provide proof before offering a person remediation - or else. There are a lot of scammers out there. I told XXXX XXXX XXXX repeatedly that if I owe a debt, I will pay it, but just because someone gives you your old phone number and address is not enough reason to have them {$1300.00} or the {$900.00} that she negotiated with the legal department to help me out. XXXX XXXX said FJS is not a debt collection company, but they are offering me a deal to avoid court - or else. Please provide me proof that I owe a valid debt and I will be happy to pay it. I am a long-term ( approx.15 years ) Citibank customer and I was dismayed by the recent monthly {$15.00} fee on my individual checking account. I also have a joint checking account with my husband. When we opened our joint checking account, we were informed that a direct deposit to any checking account with my name on it would make me eligible for fee-free checking. 

My husband and I receive two regular direct deposits ( one monthly, one bi-monthly ) into our joint checking account. Each of our individual accounts is linked to our joint account. Neither of our individual checking accounts receives a monthly direct deposit. 

I have never been charged a service fee in all my years of banking with Citi until XX/XX/2024 when I first saw a {$15.00} charge to my individual checking account. I called Citi customer service and was assured by the representative that the fee was charged in error, and it was waived. Then in XX/XX/2024, the {$15.00} fee appeared again. This time, when I called customer service, I was informed that the fee was not an error, that the previous customer service representative had given me false information, and further, that unless I initiated a direct deposit into my individual checking account, the {$15.00} fee would be levied monthly, though she waived it for me as courtesy for the month of XXXX. 

This second customer service representative also told me that when Citi shifted my account to simplified banking, they had instituted an initiation grace period during which they waived all fees. She said the grace period was now over and the fee structure was now in effect, therefore every individual checking account that did not have a direct deposit of {$250.00} would be charged $ XXXX. 

This was in direct contradiction, not only to the information given to me by the first customer service representative on the phone, but also to the information given to me by my local branch representative when I opened the joint account with my husband. 

When I pointed out that Citibank had essentially changed the rules in order to levy arbitrary fees, she claimed that the criteria for simplified banking had always been thus : Every individual checking account must have a regular direct deposit of a minimum of {$250.00}. She suggested I create a XXXX account to pay myself monthly, since transferring money from XXXX Citi account to another would not count as direct deposit. This struck me not only as contradictory but also ridiculous and convoluted, so I went to my local branch to inquire. ( Address : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/XXXX, NY XXXX ) At my local branch, I was reassured in-person that a direct deposit into one account with my name on it was the ONLY criteria required for fee-free checking. But I wanted proof of reassurance, as I explained to the service representative that I do not want to see this charge next month or any subsequent months. After consulting with a colleague, the service representative regretfully informed me that although it made no sense, and although I had not been notified of the change, the simplified banking rules had indeed changed, and I would no longer be eligible for fee-free banking unless I instituted direct deposits into every checking account. He encouraged me to raise my overall balance to {$30000.00} ( together with my husband, to become a premium members ) and thus avoid all fees. But this, of course, means moving thousands of dollars into Citibank which offers virtually no return on the money during an inflationary timetherefore Id be essentially losing money. 

My husband also has an individual checking account into which there is no direct deposit ( since we steer our income deposits into our joint account ), yet Citi is not charging him a XX/XX/XXXX monthly fee. The question arises : why is the policy inconsistently applied? And why have I been given such inconsistent answers? 

My husband has banked with Citi for 40 years. Ive been a Citi customer for over a decade. We have checking, savings, CD accounts and credit cards with Citi. 

To adhere to the new rules Citibank has arbitrarily initiated, we could change our direct deposits so that we each have funds going into our individual accounts. However, this would mean that our joint account will no longer be receiving direct deposits and will therefore begin accruing the monthly fee. Wee can figure out possible workarounds ( creating XXXX accounts & paying each other, splitting income payroll into separate accounts ). But why should we have to? This process feels onerous, complicated and unnecessarythe opposite of simplified banking. It seems like a way for Citi to fleece its customers. 



Finding another financial institution may be a complicated process for consumers like myself and my husband, but its certainly a viable option, and perhaps not as complicated as simplified banking with Citi.

Chase Bank, however, against professional practice and common sense, failed to conduct a sound and appropriate investigation, and relied unreservedly on XXXX 's claim to dictate having " found '' that I had authorized the transactions.

I am facing financial harassment and severe damage to my credit due to actions by the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, UT XXXX, regarding an alleged debt from XX/XX/XXXX. They are deliberately communicating with credit reporting agencies to harm my credit, which is negatively impacting my low-income family 's ability to thrive, particularly as a XXXX individual. 

It's important to note that federal laws, including the XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX and the XXXX XXXX, provide protections for qualified individuals with XXXX. In addition, under New York law, the statute of limitations for consumer debt is 3 years. This means that creditors or debt collectors have a maximum of 3 years to attempt to collect on an unpaid debt or initiate legal action. Once this time period has lapsed, the debt is considered time-barred. 

The New York Consumer Credit Fairness Act ( CCFA ), which came into effect on XX/XX/XXXX, governs such limitations. It applies to both original creditors like credit card companies and debt collectors. Amendments to the New York Civil Practice Laws reinforce these regulations. Importantly, once the statute of limitations has expired, it can not be reinstated or extended, even if payments are made or acknowledgment of the debt is provided. 

For debt buyers and collection agencies to pursue legal action, they must demonstrate ownership of the debt and the right to sue for its collection. This entails providing a complete chain of custody for the debt, even if it has been transferred through multiple entities. Failure to prove ownership will result in the dismissal of the case. I want the CFPB to publish this description on consumerfinance.gov so that others can learn from my horrific experience.

I asked if I needed to do anything to secure this promotion and they said that I did not and that all I needed to do was make a purchase. 

I then purchased a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX from Cabelas. I chose to use the financing because I have a high interest savings account where I could continue to earn interest, while paying off a large purchase over 12 months at 0 % interest. After making my initial payment, I called the same customer service number ( XXXX ) on XX/XX/year> to confirm they received my payment and that I was all set to continue paying the promotional rate.

They confirmed the record of my XX/XX/XXXX call, and I was told by several supervisors that even though I was provided incorrect information, there was nothing that could be done if I did not pay the full balance, I would then be charged interest on my purchase. 

To add insult to injury, two of the supervisors I spoke with had no remorse, and one insinuated that I didnt read the letter correctly. I was told the best that could be done was that they would coach the rep who provided me incorrect information. I dont blame the supervisors, the reality is that they clearly dont have the resources to do right by customers based on Capital Ones own communications.

Then when I was responsible and called to confirm the rug was pulled out from under me, with no recourse. 

Not only have you lost a Capital One customer, but Cabelas has lost a customer. More importantly, I hope you understand that I write you not to do anything for me, but in the hopes that you will review these practices so that some other customer isnt taken advantage of like I was. 

Best, XXXX XXXX
